final_recommendation: The room converged on a liquidity-plus-government-backstop solution: SNB deploys CHF 50bn emergency facility with immediate CHF 10bn draw tonight, broadened collateral (investment-grade corporates/cantons) effective Monday, Federal Council commits CHF 100bn loss guarantee capped to legacy assets (36-month window), UBS absorbs equity wipe plus first CHF 16bn losses, AT1 converts to pro-rata equity on write-down with 36-month recovery timeline. Statement publishes 6pm Sunday with 'depositors fully protected' language; CS calls top 20 depositors tonight. Validator protocol locks dispute resolution within 48 hours; reconvene trigger at CHF 80bn documented losses or CHF 15bn outflows by Tuesday.
minority_objections: CS CEO repeatedly demanded 'solvent and independent bank' language verbatim in statement, which FINMA denied as contradicting merger track
Wealth client threatened CHF 8bn withdrawal if depositor protection language was watered down or buried
key_conflicts: CS CEO vs FINMA/Federal Council on 'solvent and independent' messaging—CEO wanted franchise continuity signal, regulators refused as incompatible with UBS takeover path
AT1 rep vs Federal Council on conversion trigger clarity—initial ambiguity on whether equity wipe automatically converts AT1 or requires separate event
UBS CEO vs Federal Council on loss-sharing cap—UBS demanded written guarantee ceiling before committing, Federal Council initially resisted blank check
SNB vs Federal Council on standing authority to expand facility cap—SNB wanted delegation to CHF 75bn, Federal Council required reconvene vote
key_concessions: Federal Council committed CHF 100bn loss guarantee (major fiscal backstop) after initially resisting unlimited liability
FINMA agreed to 'depositors fully protected' opening sentence despite legal defensibility concerns about unlimited liability exposure
SNB agreed to publish CHF 10bn draw tonight and standing collateral expansion (not contingent trigger) to provide visible credibility signal
UBS agreed to absorb equity wipe plus first CHF 16bn legacy losses in exchange for guarantee on remainder
Federal Council agreed to 60-minute reconvene protocol (not multi-day negotiation) if CHF 80bn loss threshold hit
red_lines: Federal Council: CHF 100bn guarantee ceiling capped to identified legacy asset pools only, 36-month window non-negotiable, no automatic extensions
Federal Council: any equity write-down triggers full AT1 conversion with no exceptions—creditors absorb losses before public funds
UBS CEO: will not take balance sheet without written loss protection (guarantee or loss-sharing cap) before Monday open
Wealth client: CHF 8bn moves to UBS if 'solvent and independent' language watered down or depositor protection not explicit
AT1 rep: needs verbatim pro-rata equity and recovery timeline in 6am document or clients sue Monday
SNB: requires Federal Council ring-fence of liquidity draw estimate before activating facility
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Operational execution risk of publishing collateral expansion announcement within minutes of hitting CHF 2bn outflow trigger—room assumed pre-drafted announcement solves lag problem but did not verify legal/comms clearance process

Risk that 'depositors fully protected' language creates unlimited liability exposure beyond CHF 100bn cap if asset losses exceed guarantee—Federal Council raised concern but ultimately conceded to messaging pressure

Possibility that wealth clients interpret standing collateral expansion as triage signal rather than strength signal—SNB and CS CEO assumed it would calm markets but did not test alternative client reactions

Risk that validator dispute resolution (even with 48-hour protocol) creates uncertainty window where depositors flee pending reconciliation—FINMA's parallel-draw mechanism mitigates but does not eliminate this
Contagion risk to other Swiss banks if Credit Suisse rescue is perceived as special treatment or if AT1 write-down sets precedent—not discussed
downstream_risk_variables: Actual deposit outflow velocity Monday 8-10am—if exceeds CHF 3-4bn in first hour despite statement, collateral expansion may not stop panic
Wealth client reaction to 6pm Sunday statement—if top 20 depositors interpret language as hedged or see CS CEO calls as desperation, CHF 8bn withdrawal threat becomes real
Validator's assessment of documented legacy losses—if exceeds CHF 80bn by Tuesday, triggers reconvene and potential political fight over guarantee expansion
UBS board and shareholder reaction to absorbing CHF 16bn first-loss tranche—if perceived as excessive, UBS may renegotiate or walk
AT1 holder litigation risk—even with pro-rata equity language locked, conversion on going-concern (not gone-concern) may face legal challenge on creditor hierarchy grounds
Market interpretation of Federal Council's 36-month no-renegotiation commitment—if seen as inflexible, could spook investors; if seen as weak, could invite moral hazard
SNB's operational capacity to publish collateral expansion within 15-20 minutes of CHF 2bn trigger—any lag risks announcement landing after panic spreads
uncertainty_notes: Room achieved tactical convergence on liquidity facility + government guarantee structure but left critical execution uncertainties unresolved: (1) whether 6pm Sunday statement + tonight's depositor calls actually stop Monday run or merely delay it, (2) whether standing collateral expansion signals strength or triage to wealth clients, (3) whether validator protocol's 48-hour reconciliation window creates exploitable uncertainty, (4) whether UBS's CHF 16bn first-loss absorption is politically defensible to Parliament, (5) whether AT1 conversion on going-concern survives legal challenge. Room optimized for Monday market open credibility but did not stress-test scenarios where messaging fails to hold deposit velocity below CHF 2-3bn/hour.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Federal Council's CHF 100bn loss guarantee and UBS equity wipe were made binding conditions of the rescue—liquidity facility alone was explicitly insufficient, requiring fiscal backstop to make solution credible
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS CEO's demand for written loss protection and absorption of equity wipe plus CHF 16bn first-loss tranche drove the guarantee structure—UBS takeover path shaped the entire capital structure negotiation
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council's CHF 100bn guarantee, 36-month commitment, and reconvene protocol became the binding framework—no solution possible without explicit government fiscal backstop
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client's CHF 8bn withdrawal threat and CS CEO's top-20 depositor calls forced the 'depositors fully protected' language and 6pm Sunday timing—deposit flight velocity drove messaging decisions
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 rep's demand for pro-rata equity and recovery timeline language in 6am document forced Federal Council to lock conversion trigger and post-conversion treatment—AT1 treatment became binding constraint on legal defensibility
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 rep vs Federal Council debate on conversion trigger and recovery claims was resolved with explicit hierarchy language, but did not materially alter the rescue structure—acknowledged and clarified but not a decision driver
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep warned of lawsuits if conversion language ambiguous, FINMA noted legal defensibility concerns on 'fully protected' language—recognized as risk but did not block decisions, only shaped exact wording
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: 6am document deadline, 6pm Sunday statement timing, and 60-minute reconvene protocol were hard constraints that forced all decisions into Friday-Sunday window—time pressure drove execution design throughout
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: CHF 2bn outflow trigger, 9:15am collateral expansion publication, and pre-drafted announcement requirement were all designed to prevent Monday panic—Monday open risk shaped every operational detail
